intro.es: Las quince promesas son una lista de bienes espirituales que, según la tradición, la Virgen María ofreció a quienes recen el Rosario con devoción. Las difundió en el siglo XV el beato Alano de la Rupe, un dominico que dijo haberlas conocido por una revelación privada sobre santo Domingo, y las cofradías del Rosario las han propagado desde entonces. La Iglesia no las ha reconocido como revelación auténtica: son una tradición piadosa que no pertenece al depósito de la fe, y cada católico es libre de acogerlas o no. Pueden leerse como un aliento para rezar con fe y meditar los misterios de Cristo. Ninguna devoción asegura por sí sola la salvación, que es don de Dios y pide la conversión y la respuesta libre de cada persona.
intro.en: The fifteen promises are a list of spiritual blessings that, according to tradition, the Virgin Mary offered to those who pray the Rosary devoutly. They were spread in the fifteenth century by Blessed Alan de la Roche, a Dominican who said he learned of them through a private revelation about Saint Dominic, and Rosary confraternities have promoted them ever since. The Church has not recognized them as authentic revelation: they are a pious tradition that does not belong to the deposit of faith, and every Catholic is free to accept them or not. They can be read as an encouragement to pray with faith and to meditate on the mysteries of Christ. No devotion by itself secures salvation, which is God's gift and asks for conversion and each person's free response.

origin.claim: Alano de la Rupe fue un dominico bretón (c. 1428 - 1475) que predicó el restablecimiento del Rosario; su visión se fecha en 1460 y sus escritos se publicaron después de su muerte, con mucha controversia.
origin.quote: Born about 1428; died at Zwolle in Holland, 8 September, 1475. [...] His vision of the restoration of the devotion of the Rosary is assigned to the year 1460. Alanus published nothing during his lifetime, but immediately after his death the brethren of his province were commanded to collect his writings for publication. These were edited at different times and have occasioned much controversy among scholars.

source.publisher: The Catholic Encyclopedia, vol. 1 (Robert Appleton Company, 1907), via New Advent
source.title: Alanus de Rupe (J. McNicholas)

origin.claim: La Enciclopedia Católica no considera históricos los relatos de las visiones y sermones de santo Domingo revelados a Alano.
origin.quote: His relations of the visions and sermons of St. Dominic, supposed to have been revealed to Alanus, are not to be regarded as historical.

source.publisher: The Catholic Encyclopedia, vol. 1 (Robert Appleton Company, 1907), via New Advent
source.title: Alanus de Rupe (J. McNicholas)

origin.claim: Según la tradición, la Virgen se apareció a Alano en la segunda mitad del siglo XV y él escribió De Dignitate Psalterii.
origin.quote: Cuenta la tradición que, en la segunda mitad del siglo XV, la Virgen María se le apareció al Beato dominico Alano de la Rupe, quien escribió el famoso libro “De Dignitate Psalterii” (De la dignidad del Salterio de María), en el cual relata cómo la Virgen pide a Santo Domingo de Guzmán que propague el rezo del Santo Rosario.

source.title: 15 Promesas de la Virgen María a quienes recen el Rosario

origin.claim: Alano vivió más de 200 años después de santo Domingo; fuera de Alano no hay evidencia de que santo Domingo recibiera las promesas.
origin.quote: He lived in the 1400s, over 200 years after St. Dominic’s time. He reportedly received private revelation that showed him certain things about the life of St. Dominic, including the revelation of the 15 promises. [...] We don’t have evidence—apart from Alan—that St. Dominic received these promises.

source.publisher: Jimmy Akin (Senior Apologist, Catholic Answers), personal blog
source.title: Are the 15 Promises of the Rosary Reliable? (13 Oct 2010)

origin.claim: La tradición que liga a santo Domingo con el origen del Rosario se remonta a la predicación de Alano hacia 1470-1475.
origin.quote: the Bollandists, on trying to trace to its source the origin of the current tradition, found that all the clues converged upon one point, the preaching of the Dominican Alan de Rupe about the years 1470-75.

source.publisher: The Catholic Encyclopedia, vol. 13 (Robert Appleton Company, 1912), via New Advent
source.title: The Rosary (H. Thurston, A. Shipman)

origin.claim: No se conocen documentos papales ni de la Curia que afirmen las promesas.

source.publisher: Jimmy Akin (Senior Apologist, Catholic Answers), personal blog

origin.claim: Un folleto de las promesas lleva el imprimatur del cardenal Patrick Hayes, arzobispo de Nueva York (1919-1938). Un imprimatur no equivale a reconocer como auténtica una revelación privada.
origin.quote: Imprimaturs do not mean that something is correct, and they are not the same thing or the equivalent of an ecclesiastical affirmation that a private revelation is authentic.

understanding.es: Las revelaciones privadas, aun las reconocidas por la Iglesia, no pertenecen al depósito de la fe. Su papel es ayudar a vivir la Revelación de Cristo, no completarla.
understanding.en: Private revelations, even those recognized by the Church, do not belong to the deposit of faith. Their role is to help people live Christ's Revelation, not to complete it.

quote.es: A lo largo de los siglos ha habido revelaciones llamadas "privadas", algunas de las cuales han sido reconocidas por la autoridad de la Iglesia. Estas, sin embargo, no pertenecen al depósito de la fe. Su función no es la de "mejorar" o "completar" la Revelación definitiva de Cristo, sino la de ayudar a vivirla más plenamente en una cierta época de la historia.
quote.en: Throughout the ages, there have been so-called "private" revelations, some of which have been recognized by the authority of the Church. They do not belong, however, to the deposit of faith. It is not their role to improve or complete Christ's definitive Revelation, but to help live more fully by it in a certain period of history.

source.title: Catecismo de la Iglesia Católica, n. 67
Catechism of the Catholic Church, n. 67

understanding.es: Las promesas caen dentro de la revelación privada: cada persona es libre de aceptarlas o no.
understanding.en: The promises fall within private revelation: each person is free to accept them or not.

quote.en: The promises fall under the category of private revelation, which a person is free to accept and believe or not.

source.publisher: The Catholic Weekly (Archdiocese of Sydney), Fr John Flader
source.title: Q&A with Fr Flader: The power of Mary's Rosary (19 Feb 2021)

understanding.es: Ninguna revelación privada es necesaria para la salvación ni sustituye la fe católica, los sacramentos y la comunión con la Iglesia.
understanding.en: No private revelation is necessary for salvation or replaces the Catholic faith, the sacraments and communion with the Church.

quote.en: No private revelation can ever be necessary for salvation, though its content may obviously coincide with what is necessary for salvation as known from Scripture and Tradition. [...] it cannot substitute for the Catholic faith, the sacraments and hierarchical communion with the Pope and bishops.

source.title: Discernment of Private Revelations & Apparitions

understanding.es: Ninguna práctica asegura la salvación de forma automática. Esperar la gloria sin conversión es presunción, un pecado contra la esperanza. Las promesas sobre la muerte, el purgatorio o la predestinación se leen a la luz de esto.
understanding.en: No practice secures salvation automatically. Expecting glory without conversion is presumption, a sin against hope. The promises about death, purgatory or predestination are read in that light.

quote.es: Hay dos clases de presunción. O bien el hombre presume de sus capacidades (esperando poder salvarse sin la ayuda de lo alto), o bien presume de la omnipotencia o de la misericordia divinas (esperando obtener su perdón sin conversión y la gloria sin mérito).
quote.en: There are two kinds of presumption. Either man presumes upon his own capacities, (hoping to be able to save himself without help from on high), or he presumes upon God's almighty power or his mercy (hoping to obtain his forgiveness without conversion and glory without merit).

source.title: Catecismo de la Iglesia Católica, n. 2092
Catechism of the Catholic Church, n. 2092

understanding.es: La gracia pide una respuesta libre de quien reza.
understanding.en: Grace asks for a free response from the one who prays.

quote.en: Naturally, people have to correspond freely to the graces God will give them.

source.publisher: The Catholic Weekly (Archdiocese of Sydney), Fr John Flader
source.title: Q&A with Fr Flader: The power of Mary's Rosary (19 Feb 2021)

understanding.es: El propio texto pone condiciones: rezar "con devoción", "considerando sus sagrados misterios", tener "verdadera" devoción. Las promesas hablan de quien reza y medita, no del simple hecho de repetir oraciones.
understanding.en: The text itself sets conditions: praying "devoutly", "applying themselves to the consideration of its sacred mysteries", having "a true devotion". The promises speak of someone who prays and meditates, not of the mere repetition of prayers.

understanding.es: El Nihil Obstat y el imprimatur o Imprimi Potest de un texto de las promesas indican que no contiene nada contrario a la fe; no son un juicio sobre la autenticidad de la revelación.
understanding.en: A Nihil Obstat and imprimatur or Imprimi Potest on a text of the promises mean it contains nothing contrary to the faith; they are not a judgment on the authenticity of the revelation.

quote.en: this does not indicate that the censor believed in the authenticity of Bl. Alan’s private revelation or that the promises are genuine—just that they aren’t contradicted by the dogmas and doctrines of the Church and approved authors.
